liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Never Trust A Woman** (2 reviews): Garcia was heading backstage after Terrapin, but Brent started singing this and Jerry returned, strapping his guitar on again; Phil took off his bass and limped backstage, then returned to his amp and played a crushing version [20][25]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this To Lay Me Down among the top ten versions [15]
- **Passenger** (1 review): Passenger, a standard first-set tune then, ripped; reviewer wonders why it was retired after the 1981 New Year's run [15]
- **Samson & Delilah** (1 review): Samson opens the second set confidently, with Bobby's restrained rhythm playing fitting well and no hesitation at the start [21]
- **Space** (1 review): During space Mickey played the beam, shaking the air as the sun set over the bay [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-09-13.148724.sbd.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 192 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1981-09-13.sbd.miller.32576.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 26 songs; 188 min; rated 3.7/5 by 10 [3]. Said about its sound: The previously circulating version was tinny with Phil washed out; reviewer says solid sources only appeared recently [19]
- **gd81-09-13.wise.munder.7092.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 25 songs; 183 min; rated 3.86/5 by 7 [4]
- **gd1981-09-13.148628.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 26 songs; 188 min [5]

## Around the show

- A Hells Angel brought his motorcycle on stage, wiped it and revved the engine during drums; it is audible on tape [17]
- The motorcycle during the drum solo was so loud it shook the listener's body; homemade hot air balloons were apparently released too [22]
- Fans stood throughout except at the break; reviewer sat on the rocks in beautiful weather, enjoying the setting sun [23]
- Weather was perfect; afterward hundreds of fans stood howling at the moon in the street outside the Greek [24]
- Reviewer noticed Phil limping in the second set, though he had not limped during the first set [25]
- Closing the first Greek run, it falls short of the previous day's monster show but is still very nice [15]
- Third night of the run: the 11th was spacey, the 12th straight-ahead jamming, this one a mellow afternoon show [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-09-13.148724.sbd.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette [1]
- **gd1981-09-13.sbd.miller.32576.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> Cassette Master -> ? -> Cassette -> Sound Forge -> CD; Set 2: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette [3]. Also: Set 1 came from Jeff Harrison and Jake Feinberg, set 2 from Walker and Scotton; Jim Wise's audience tape used for patching; Sennheiser 421 cassette master patches fill Jack Straw, Loser, Terrapin Station, Never Trust A Woman and Drums [3]
- **gd81-09-13.wise.munder.7092.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [4]. Also: Jim Wise taped with Sennheiser 421 mics into a Sony TC D-5; passed via Nic Brokenleg and Kevin Gills; Willy did EAC/SHN [4]
- **gd1981-09-13.148628.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; 3 x Nakamichi 700 mics (cardioid left & right - X pattern; 80 degree angle; 6db bass EQ, omni center pointed… [5]
